describes: The settings of single tools: how much of a failing job's output the git hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints (`gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`); and the agents' GitHub App, its installation, the one repository a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach and the account that owns it, which the dev container clones, how much of a kept token's hour must be left for it to hand the token out again, and the App's bot account the dev container commits as (`githubApp*`).
whyThisFileExists: Each of these belongs to one tool, unlike the rest of the policy, and a constant a tool reads still lives in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it (`AGENTS.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth). They share one record under `policy/` rather than one beside each tool, so every tunable of the workflow is in one directory.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run hooks:selftest holds `gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`: it refuses a policy without the key, and asserts that a failing job's printed output stops at the key's value while a file holds all of it; the runner refuses to start a commit or a push without the key or its `Means` sibling. mise run github-app-token:selftest holds the seven `githubApp*` keys. It runs `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh`'s `clone`, which reads `githubAppRepositoryOwner` and `githubAppTokenRepository` for the clone it makes at a container's first start, against a local repository at the address they give, and refuses with its reason a policy without the owner or with the placeholder in its place. It also refuses a policy without `githubAppId` or `githubAppTokenRepository`, or with a `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` of 0, by its reason; it holds the identity `identity` prints as made, in GitHub's noreply form, from `githubAppBotLogin` and `githubAppBotUserId`, whatever their values, and refuses a policy without either; it holds the JSON Web Token as signed for the App `githubAppId` names, and the request as made for the installation `githubAppInstallationId` names and for the one repository the policy names, before a stub of GitHub's endpoint; and it holds a kept token with less than `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` left as replaced. Its fixtures name an App, a bot account, a repository and an owner of their own, so it holds the code independently of this record's named placeholders. App ids accept JSON numbers or positive decimal strings; unresolved placeholders and malformed ids are refused. No gate holds the App's two ids to GitHub, which only a token minted from the App's key can read, nor the bot account's login and id, which GitHub's users endpoint gives, nor the owner to the repository's.
provenance: Came with the template this repository was bootstrapped from; each key's `Means` gives the reason for its value.
gitHooksFailedOutputBytesMeans: The most bytes of a failing job's output that the hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints at a commit, a push or `mise run gates`: the last ones, where a failure's summary is, followed by the path of a file under the temporary directory that holds all of it. A passing job prints one line. Without it one failing job can print past what an agent's tool output holds: a run with one failing job once printed 110,244 bytes under lefthook, and the harness cut it mid-run. Sized from a passing run in which the largest job printed 23,593 bytes, the next two 9,590 and 9,331, and every other under 7 KB, so three failures print about 25 KB. Raising it shows more of a large failure in one read; lowering it fits more failures in one. Where it loses: a long job failing on an early case, whose FAIL line sits more than 8 KB before its end, needs a second read of the file, where no cap would have shown it at once.
githubAppIdMeans: The id of the agents' GitHub App, which `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` puts as the `iss` of the JSON Web Token it signs with the App's private key when it asks GitHub for an installation token for the dev container's `git` and `gh`. Read from the App's settings page. GitHub checks the token's signature against the public key of the App this names, so a wrong id, or another App's with this App's key, gets every token refused, and the helper prints GitHub's answer. Deploy fills this named placeholder for the Target project; until then the helper refuses it.
githubAppBotLoginMeans: The login of the agents' GitHub App's bot account, which the dev container commits as: `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` prints it as `user.name`, and `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` sets that in the container's `~/.gitconfig` at start when no `user.email` is set. Read from GitHub's users endpoint, `gh api /users/<login>` with `[bot]` written `%5Bbot%5D`, which gives the account's type as Bot. A wrong login gives commits a name that is not the App's, while `githubAppBotUserId` still ties them to the account through the email. Where it loses: an App renamed on GitHub keeps committing under the old name until this is edited, and a container whose `~/.gitconfig` was set before the edit keeps it until a rebuild discards that file, since the entrypoint leaves an email already set.
githubAppBotUserIdMeans: The id of that bot account, not the App's id (`githubAppId`): `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` makes `user.email` from it as `<this>+<githubAppBotLogin>@users.noreply.github.com`, the form GitHub documents for an account's noreply address (docs.github.com, "Email addresses reference", read 2026-10-06). GitHub attributes a commit with that email to the bot account, through a rename too, since the id is in it. Read from the same users endpoint as the login. Where it loses: a commit is not signed by it, so GitHub shows no Verified badge on the container's commits, which only a commit the App creates through the API gets.
githubAppInstallationIdMeans: The installation of that App whose installation token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` asks for at `/app/installations/<this>/access_tokens`. A token asked for with no body reaches every repository the installation covers, so the helper asks for `githubAppTokenRepository` alone; narrowing the installation itself to that repository, in its settings on GitHub, closes what a token minted with no body could reach, which the helper cannot. Read from the App's settings page. Where it loses: an App uninstalled and installed again gets a new id, and every token is refused until this is edited.
githubAppTokenRepositoryMeans: The bootstrapped project sets this to its own repository's bare name; `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` refuses the placeholder as not a repository's bare name, and `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` clones nothing while it stands. The one repository, by its bare name, that a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach: it sends `{"repositories": [<this>]}` with each request, which GitHub documents as narrowing that one token to the repositories named, among those the installation covers (docs.github.com, "Create an installation access token for an app", read 2026-10-06). This repository, since the dev container's sessions work here and its tracker's Dolt remote is here too (`.beads/config.yaml`). Without it, every token reaches every repository the installation covers (`githubAppInstallationIdMeans`). Where it loses: it narrows the tokens the helper mints, and no other: a session can read the App's key, which the container mounts for it, and mint a token for every repository the installation covers, so the installation should cover this repository alone. A repository later added to the installation on GitHub is open to such a token at once, and no gate reads the installation's list to see it.
githubAppRepositoryOwnerMeans: The bootstrapped project sets this to the account that owns its repository; `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` refuses the placeholder and clones nothing while it stands. The account that owns `githubAppTokenRepository`, which the App is installed on. `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` clones `https://github.com/<this>/<githubAppTokenRepository>.git` into the container's workspace volume at its first start, with no token, so the repository must be public for that clone. It reads both keys from the copy of this record `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` puts in the image, because the clone that holds this file does not exist yet. A changed value reaches a container only once it is rebuilt, and only one whose volume holds no clone yet. Where it loses: a wrong value clones another account's code into every new container, where the entrypoint runs `npm ci` and its hooks.
githubAppTokenRefreshSecondsMeans: How many seconds of a kept installation token's life must be left for `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` to hand it out again; with fewer, it mints a fresh one and keeps that. GitHub's installation token lasts an hour (docs.github.com, "Generating an installation access token for a GitHub App", read 2026-10-06), and `git` and `gh` each read a token once, when a command starts, so a command must end before the token it read expires. 1800 gives every command at least half an hour, which holds a watcher run in the background, such as `gh pr checks --watch` while `verify` runs, and costs one call to GitHub each half hour a session works. Raising it toward 3600 mints more often, at 3599 once for every command; lowering it hands out a token a long command outlives. Where it loses: one `gh` or `git` command that runs longer than half an hour, started as its token's last half hour began, is refused midway, where a shorter-lived command, or a token minted afresh, would not be.
